The queue-with-backoff approach fits the ticket: deliveries are stored, retried for 24 hours and visible to the customer. One thing blocks the merge and two should be fixed with it.

### Blocker · F1 · A retried delivery is sent without an idempotency key

A retry re-sends the same payload with no key, so a customer whose endpoint accepted the first attempt slowly receives the event twice. See `jobs/DeliverWebhook.php:58`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Attempt 1 times out"] --> B["Endpoint still processes it"]
  B --> C["Attempt 2 sends again"]
  C --> D["Two events for one"]
  class D bad
  classDef bad fill:#FCE9D9,stroke:#6B2F04,color:#6B2F04
```

<details>
<summary>Proof: a throwaway test, two deliveries for one event</summary>

```php
$event = Event::factory()->create();
DeliverWebhook::dispatchSync($event);   // times out; the endpoint commits anyway
DeliverWebhook::dispatchSync($event);   // no key, so the endpoint commits again
$this->assertSame(1, $endpoint->countReceived($event->id));  // got 2
```

</details>

### Should · F2 · No way to replay a delivery after the window closes

After 24 hours a delivery is marked dead and nothing can send it again. Acceptance criterion 3 on ABC-231 asks the customer to recover from a long outage.

### Should · F3 · The failure test passes with the retry code reverted

I reverted the retry and `tests/WebhookRetryTest.php:31` still passed, so it does not pin the behaviour.

**Not checked:** worker behaviour across a deploy restart; production delivery volumes.

Whole cents is the right representation and the migration is in the right order. One export path blocks the merge.

### Blocker · F1 · The CSV export still divides by 100 twice

`app/Invoice.php:102` divides the stored cents, and `ExportInvoices` divides the result again. An exported total of `12.34` comes out as `0.1234`.

### Should · F2 · The migration has no down path for the decimal column

`database/migrations/2026_09_30_invoices.php:18` drops the old column without recreating it, so the migration cannot be rolled back on a release that has to go backwards.

### Should · F3 · The rounding test asserts on a value it computed the same way

`tests/InvoiceTotalTest.php:44` builds the expected total with the same helper it is testing, so the test cannot fail if the helper is wrong.

**Not checked:** the reporting warehouse reads the same column and was not looked at.

**Not checked:** cache behaviour across two processes; the test runs in one.

Splitting per tenant with a cursor is the right shape. Two things should be fixed with it.

### Should · F1 · A partial export leaves the previous file in place

`jobs/ExportTenant.php:40` writes in place, so a failed run leaves yesterday's file looking like today's.

### Should · F2 · The cursor is held in memory, so a restart starts the tenant again

A restart re-runs the tenant from the beginning. For the largest tenant that is most of the window.

**Not checked:** the bucket's lifecycle rules were not read, so the stale-file cleanup is assumed.

draft.body:
The change does what the ticket asks and the shape is right: the scheduled path builds its own context and the branch is out of `ReportBuilder`. One blocker, and it is the composition of two reasonable-looking decisions rather than either of them.

### Blocker · F9 · The column policy is skipped entirely when the definition names no columns

Two decisions compose here. The array cast answers `[]` for a null column, and this early return reads `[]` as “no policy” — so a definition older than the migration exports every column, including the two its tenant's policy hides. Eleven definitions in staging are in that state with an active schedule.

### Should · F1 · An empty allowed-columns list means every column, not none

`allowed_columns` arrives here as `[]` for any definition whose column was never written, and every reader downstream treats an empty list as “nothing to narrow”. `ColumnPolicy::for()` already draws the distinction the web path needs; this path could call it.

### Should · F3 · A schedule whose tenant row has gone is dispatched anyway

A schedule whose tenant row is gone is dispatched and then fails inside `ExportContext::forSchedule` with a null dereference, four frames deep. Filtering the dispatch query on the tenant's existence makes the same failure readable.

### Should · F6 · The policy is applied after the query is built, so a hidden column is still selected

The policy narrows rows that are already in memory, so the hidden columns are selected and read before they are dropped. `ReportBuilder::withPolicy()` narrows the `select` instead.

### Should · F11 · The web path builds its context from the request with no tenant check

The removed branch called `ReportPolicy::view()` before building the context, and the call went with it. `download()` still authorises; `stream()`, reachable from the signed-URL route added in #496, does not.

### Should · F13 · A soft-deleted tenant is exported; only a hard-deleted one is skipped

The guard skips the job and not the schedule: `next_run_at` is advanced before the job runs, so a trashed tenant's schedule is dispatched and skipped every night. Schedule 118 has done that 39 times since September with no audit row to show for it.

### Should · F14 · The description does not say what happens to an export that is skipped

Three of the change's early returns each decide what an export produces, and none of them appears in the description. Three sentences under “What is skipped” would answer the question a reader otherwise has to read the job for.

### Question · F5 · Two schedules for one tenant at once would write the audit entry twice

Can two schedules for one tenant be due in the same minute? Both would write an audit row keyed on the tenant and the date, and the unique index on that pair was dropped in #502.

### Question · F7 · Nothing says what happens to a schedule whose definition was deleted

A schedule whose definition has been deleted releases back to the queue and is retried until the attempt limit, then dispatched again the next night. Is deactivating it the intended answer?

### Question · F12 · Whether the audit entry still fits is not established

`RecordsAnExport` is outside this change, and the scheduled path passes it a system actor with no id. Is `export_audit.actor_id` nullable, and does its consumer read a null actor as a system export?

### Nit · F4 · The class is named for the direction, not for what it makes

The two siblings in this namespace are named for what they return. This one is named for the direction of the conversion, so it does not read with them.

### Nit · F10 · The removed branch leaves a comment describing it

The branch this comment describes was removed four lines above.

**Not checked.** The reporting front end, which reads the same definitions but was not changed.

held_back.claim: The superseded accessor `TenantContext::tenantForRequest()` is still public with nothing marking it superseded, so the next person who needs a tenant reads the accessor that is still there, reaches for the obvious name, and writes a second call path into the export code this change exists to remove — and because the `@deprecated` annotation is what the static analyser reads, that second caller is found in review by somebody rather than failing the build on the way in.
